q: 1. Which of the following represent an activity?
explain: Construction of foundation, roof, and superstructure are all time- and resource-consuming tasks, hence all represent activities.

q: 2. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are assumed to follow a Beta distribution.

q: 3. Earliest finish of an activity is always
options: greater than earliest event time of the following node
less than earliest event time of the following node
less than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
greater than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
explain: The earliest finish time of an activity must be less than or equal to the earliest event time of the node it leads into (since the node's earliest time is set by the latest-finishing predecessor).

q: 4. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule, often caused by resource shortages or delays.

q: 5. In the network shown in Fig., activity 4-5 can be started only when
explain: From the given network, node 4 is reached only after both activities 2-4 and 3-4 are complete, so activity 4-5 requires both to finish first.

q: 6. A stage or point where all previous jobs merging in it are completed and all further jobs bursting out are still to be completed is known as a
explain: This describes a node in the network, which is technically an event.

q: 7. In PERT technique, completion of an activity is called
explain: In PERT, the completion point of an activity is termed the head event.

q: 8. Earliest finish time of an activity is always
options: equal to or more than earliest event time of the following node
equal to or less than earliest event time of the following node
more than earliest time of the following node
explain: Earliest finish time is equal to or less than the earliest event time of the following node[cite: 1].

q: 9. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: To ensure no following activities are delayed, the latest allowable time is the minimum of the late finishes of succeeding activities minus their durations.

q: 10. Which of the following is a PERT event?
explain: 'Concreting of roof completed' denotes an instantaneous milestone/state, qualifying as a PERT event, unlike the ongoing transport/formwork processes.

q: 11. SLACK time refers to an
explain: Slack is specifically associated with events (the difference between $T_L$ and $T_E$), while 'float' is associated with activities.

q: 12. The technique which is activity oriented is
explain: CPM is activity-oriented, focusing on individual activities and their durations, unlike PERT which is event-oriented.

q: 13. The minimum number of years required to complete any research project may be
explain: Research projects have variable timelines depending on complexity and findings.

q: 14. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' represents a completed milestone/state (an event), while the others describe ongoing activities.

q: 15. An event is indicated on the network by a number enclosed in
explain: While circles are standard, various shapes like squares or ellipses can be used to represent nodes in different conventions.

q: 16. Which of the following is an activity

q: 17. Slack time in PERT analysis
options: can never be greater than zero
is always zero for critical activities
can never be less than zero
explain: Critical events are those on the path with the least amount of slack (zero or negative).

q: 18. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of preceding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float specifically identifies how much an activity can be delayed without affecting the float or start of the succeeding activity.

q: 19. The free float affects only
explain: Free float affects preceding activities/successor relationships as per definition[cite: 1].

q: 20. The area under the beta-curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) is the mean of the distribution, which bisects the area under the probability curve.

q: 21. For a curve, larger the variance
explain: Variance is a measure of spread; a higher variance means the actual time could deviate significantly from the mean, increasing uncertainty.

q: 24. The activity which is crashed first has
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: Crashing follows a least-cost approach, starting with the critical activity having the least (lowest) cost slope to minimize the additional cost incurred.

q: 25. The figure indicates

q: 26. In a CPM/PERT network, the number of event is
options: more than the number of activity
equal to the number of activity
explain: The relationship between the number of events and activities depends entirely on the network topology and the use of dummy activities.

q: 27. The technique used for the management and development of Polaris Missile in American Navy Force is
explain: PERT was famously developed by the US Navy in the late 1950s specifically for the Polaris missile project.

q: 28. Positive slack indicates
explain: Positive slack means there is extra time available, implying the project or event is ahead of its required deadline.

q: 29. In resource levelling
options: total duration of project is reduced
total duration of project is increased
uniform demand of resources is achieved
explain: Resource levelling aims to smooth out resource demand fluctuations over the project duration, achieving a more uniform resource requirement, potentially extending duration.

q: 30. The slack for an event i is given by
explain: Slack for an event is calculated as the Latest Allowable occurrence time ($T_L$) minus the Earliest Expected occurrence time ($T_E$).

q: 31. A dummy activity is that part of the project which
explain: A dummy activity has zero duration and consumes no resources; it exists only to maintain correct network logic.

q: 32. Variance is
options: Sum of time duration / number of jobs
difference between time and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviation
explain: Mathematically, variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean.

q: 33. In PERT analysis is the duration of the activities is taken as
explain: PERT uses the expected (mean) time, calculated from the three estimates, as the duration for each activity in scheduling calculations.

q: 34. The square root of the variance is known as
explain: By definition, the standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

q: 35. In PERT technique the critical path has slack equal to
explain: By definition, the critical path (in both PERT and CPM) always has zero slack/float.

q: 36. t^{ij} and t_E^{ij} indicates the time required for completion of an activity in CPM and PERT respectively. Here the subscript E stands for
explain: In PERT, subscript E denotes the expected time accounting for uncertainty[cite: 1].

q: 37. The variance will be zero if
explain: Variance is only zero if all data points (durations) are exactly equal to the mean.

q: 38. The variance of the PERT critical path is equal to
options: sum of variance of activities lying on critical path
maximum of sum of variances upto end event
minimum of sum of variances upto end event
explain: The variance of the project completion time equals the sum of the variances of all activities lying on the critical path.

q: 39. The CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is difference in the planned & actual performance
explain: Network updating is triggered whenever actual progress deviates from the planned schedule, requiring re-planning to reflect current status.

q: 40. Crash project duration is obtained by adding the
options: crash durations for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities along the critical path
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path
explain: The total crashed duration is the sum of the crash times of all activities forming the critical path.

q: 41. The Bar chart Technique is commonly used because it
options: is simple to draw & easy to understand
is useful for cost & quality control
explain: Bar charts are popular due to their simplicity, clear progress indication, and usefulness in monitoring cost and quality - all reasons apply.

q: 42. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for
explain: PERT was developed for and is best suited to large, complex projects with uncertain activity durations.

q: 43. A frequency distribution curve
options: having single lump is called unimodal curve
if symmetrical is called normal curve
if unsymmetrical is called skew curve
explain: These are standard statistical terms describing the shape and symmetry of frequency distributions.

q: 44. The pictorial representation of activity and event of a project is known as
explain: The pictorial diagram showing activities and events with their interrelationships in a project is called a network diagram.

q: 45. If the completion time for a particular project is 6 weeks and its expected time is 8 weeks, then the slack time for the project is
explain: Slack time is calculated as (Scheduled Time - Expected Time). Here, 6 weeks - 8 weeks = -2 weeks. Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule.

q: 46. If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earliest start and earliest finish time, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, then following relation holds good
explain: In network analysis, finish times are the start times plus duration, and start times are finish times minus duration. All these formulas correctly represent the relationships between activity timings.

q: 47. Technical planning is carried out for the
options: planning resource and initiating procurement action
explain: Technical planning encompasses preparing detailed drawings, estimates, and resource/procurement planning - all these activities together.

q: 48. An activity is
explain: An activity in a project network is a specific portion of work that consumes time and resources to complete.

q: 49. If \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3 \dots are the standard deviations of completion for the activities along the critical path, the standard deviations of the time of completion of the project is given by
explain: Standard deviation for the total project duration is computed using the square root of variances[cite: 1].

q: 50. Total project time is the
options: sum of duration of all activities
sum of duration of non-critical activities
sum of duration of critical activities
explain: The total project duration is determined by the length of the critical path, which is the sequence of activities with the longest total duration.
